newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Manufacturing drives Taiwan Dec industry recovery.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing drives Taiwan Dec industry recovery.

text.p: Taiwan's industrial output in December rose a higher-than-expected 6.11 percent compared with December 1995 chiefly on the strength of recovering second-half manufacturing, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
The strong December uptick helped ensure that 1996 full-year industrial output growth would be positive. Industrial output in 1996 grew 1.70 percent compared with 1995, the ministry said.
The December output figure came in sharply higher than the average 2.99 percent projection that resulted from a January 16 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.

The ministry attributed the December rise to a recovery in manufacturing output. The manufacturing index, including metals, machinery, information electronics, chemical and consumer products, rose 7.48 percent in December from a year earlier.

Consistently high manufacturing output in the second half of 1997 contributed to year-on-year rise in industrial output of 3.68 percent in the six months, which helped compensate for a 0.34 percent decline in the first six months, it said.
The 1.70 percent full-year industrial output rise also reflected an improving second-half economy, the ministry said.
Real estate and construction industry output fell 23.62 percent in December and 17.44 percent for all of 1996.
Mining industry output was down 4.87 percent in December and 5.30 percent for 1996.
